rows.text: Pluto takes about twenty years to cross a sign, so this is an era, not a mood. In Aquarius it goes to work on power itself: who holds it, who it runs through, and how much of it now lives in networks, machines, and crowds instead of a few hands at the top. The systems we treat as permanent are exactly the ones being quietly rebuilt.

For close to two decades, this transit rewires how power moves through action. You notice it in the abrupt pivot at meetings, the sudden decision to cut through red tape, the flare-ups when patience runs out. Everyone feels the push to act directly and reshape their corner of the world with speed, not delay.

For two decades, Pluto moves through the house of deep feeling and protection. We watch people rebuild their closest bonds like architects demolishing walls to pour new foundations. It shows up in how fiercely we guard what matters - from childhood wounds to home rituals - while quietly shifting those same grounds underfoot. You’ll see it in the way a parent redraws boundaries with a grown child or how a friend’s loyalty hardens into something unyielding yet fragile.
